reason: Removes the --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning flag from the two hook commands, per decision-6 AC #2 ('no --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning left in scripts, hooks or .claude/settings.json'). No-op removal: the flag only suppressed a Node warning, and the Node 24 move this task makes elsewhere means the warning no longer fires anyway.
Same flag removal as the .claude/settings.json override, in the pre-commit staged-check step. No-op: changes no check behaviour.

TASK-24: pins all three jobs' runs-on from ubuntu-latest to ubuntu-24.04, urgent because GitHub moves the ubuntu-latest label to 26 this week (DRAFT-1, filed from the TASK-1.40/1.41 review). Hardens CI, does not weaken it: the existing version-bump exemption (isVersionBumpPair) only recognises 'uses: owner/repo@vN' and '*-version:' lines, and normalizeDigits cannot match 'latest' against '24.04' as a digit-only change, so this specific diff trips the line-removal finding with no automatic exemption.

TASK-37: the literal 'run: pnpm -s test' line becomes 'run: node tools/hooks/unit-tests.ts', a wrapper that skips the suite only when every staged file is under backlog/ and runs it unchanged otherwise. Not a loosening in substance (a pure board change cannot break a test), but the line-removal heuristic cannot tell that apart from an actual loosening. Bruk approved the board-only skip explicitly before this was written.
Same pin as the ci.yml override (TASK-24), for the one job that must share its runner image and Chromium with ci.yml's browser pass (R42, decision-11) - the two would silently drift apart otherwise.

Removes the Stop hook (R56) entry. Bruk asked directly for this (it re-ran checks/typecheck/tests after every agent turn, slowing live device-testing iteration) - a deliberate, explicit removal of enforcement, not a loophole. tools/hooks/stop.ts stays in the repo, just unregistered, so it can be wired back in later without rewriting it.
